# 2 Baruch Chapter 18 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 18:2 — "untimely death" vs. "premature death"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "untimely-death" | Literal compound; "untimely" for Syriac b'l-zimna |
| LOGOS | "untimely death" | Formal |
| PNEUMA | "premature death" | "Premature" is more common in modern usage |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** LOGOS adopted. "Untimely death" is the established rendering (Charles, Klijn) for the Syriac concept of death as an intrusion that came before its proper time. "Premature" is acceptable but medical in register.

---

## 18:2 — "each one has prepared for his own soul torment to come"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "each-one-of-them-has-prepared-for-his-own-soul torment-to-come" | Literal |
| LOGOS | "each one of them has prepared for his own soul torment to come" | Formal |
| PNEUMA | "each person has been responsible for preparing his own suffering" | "Responsible for" adds moral judgment; "suffering" for "torment" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** LOGOS adopted. "Torment to come" is more eschatologically specific than PNEUMA's "suffering" — the Syriac term refers to the future judgment torment, not present suffering.

---

**Total disagreements this chapter: 2**
